input.question: Why does a youtube video load faster than a gif?
input.ground_truth: So many trolls, and nobody got it right yet. GIFs weren't designed for animation. [Source (Look at Appendix D. Conventions)](_URL_0_). On the other hand, video was designed for animation. For this reason, in a GIF file, each frame is transmitted entirely, while in a video file, only the differences between frames are transmitted. Also, modern video formats use better compression than GIF, but that's not as important. (Disclaimer: I'm not highly knowledgeable about this topic and I may have got something wrong. But this is surely better than the other answers.).

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why does a youtube video load faster than a gif?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you are trying to fill a small cup with water and a big bathtub with water.

A **YouTube video** is like the big bathtub. But when you want to watch a video, YouTube only sends you a little bit of water (a little bit of the video) at a time, just enough to keep the video playing smoothly. It’s like someone is carefully pouring water into the tub so you can start taking a bath right away, instead of waiting for the whole tub to fill up.

A **GIF** is like trying to pour all the water from a big bucket into your small cup at once. But GIFs are actually a bunch of pictures put together and played very fast. When you want to see a GIF, your computer has to download all those pictures before it can start showing them to you. It’s like waiting for the whole bucket to empty into your cup before you can see any water.

That’s why a YouTube video starts playing faster than a GIF—you get to see a little bit of the video right away, but with a GIF, you have to wait for everything to come before you see anything move!
